steps.scene: A narrow street lined with parked cars. In one of them, someone is sitting in the driver's seat.

question.prompt: What should you be ready for?

options.text: Glare bouncing off their windscreen
Their door opening into your path
Nothing — a parked car can't be a hazard

question.explanation: Someone sitting in a parked car is about to get out. Slow down, leave room, and watch that door.

steps.title: Look for what's hidden
steps.body: A hazard is anything that may make you change speed or direction. Scan far ahead, close in, and your mirrors — not just the car in front.

question.prompt: Where should most of your attention be?

options.text: Well ahead, so you meet hazards early
On the bumper of the car in front
On your speedometer

question.explanation: Looking well ahead buys you time. React to what's developing, not to what has already happened.

steps.scene: A residential street. Cars are parked nose to tail and an ice-cream van has stopped on the far side.

options.text: Children may run out between the parked cars
The van driver will wave you through
The children will see you and wait

question.explanation: You can't see a child between parked cars until they're in the road. Ease off and cover the brake.

steps.scene: A bus is stopped at a bus stop ahead of you. The last person in the queue has just stepped aboard.

options.text: The bus will wait until you've passed
The bus may signal and pull out
The bus will stay put for several minutes

question.explanation: Once the last passenger boards, the bus is ready to move. Give way if you safely can, and watch for people crossing in front.

steps.scene: You're following a cyclist on a wet road. Ahead of them is a line of metal drain covers close to the kerb.

options.text: The cyclist will stop and dismount
The cyclist may swerve out to avoid them
The cyclist will hold their line, so you can pass close

question.explanation: Wet metal is slippery, so riders steer around it. Stay back and give a cyclist room to move out.

steps.title: When you can't see
steps.body: At a junction with a blocked view, creep forward until you can see. The traffic on the main road can't see you either.

question.prompt: Your view emerging from a junction is blocked by a hedge. What do you do?

options.text: Edge out slowly until you can see clearly
Pull out quickly to get it over with
Sound your horn and go

question.explanation: Pull forward slowly until you can see up and down the road. If you don't know it's clear, don't go.

steps.wrongBelief: Good reactions make up for not looking far ahead.

options.text: It's right — quick reactions are all that matter
You still travel while you react, so late is late
Reactions have nothing to do with driving

question.explanation: Thinking distance is real distance. Spotting a hazard early is what gives you room to deal with it.

steps.repairNote: Reacting quickly still costs you thinking distance. Planning early is what keeps the gap you need.
